195.subject: Botany
195.text:
Assertion : Meiosis II is similar to mitosis. 
Reason : Meiosis I cannot occur in haploid cells.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false
195.sol: Meiosis consists of two divisions, meiosis I and meiosis II. The first division of meiosis is called heterotypic or reduction division. During this division the number of chromosomes is reduced to half. The two chromatids of a chromosome become genetically different due to crossing over. These chromatids are separated in the second division of meiosis. The second meiotic division is known as homotypic or equational division, because the chromosome number remains the same as produced after the end of the first division. Though meiosis II is similar to mitosis, meiosis II is not mitosis because (i) it always occurs in haploid cells, (ii) it is not preceded by DNA replication, (iii) the two chromatids of a chromosome are often dissimilar, (iv) the daughter cells formed after meiosis II are neither similar to each other nor similar to the parent cell.
195.meta: Assertion : Meiosis II is similar to mitosis. Reason : Meiosis I cannot occur in haploid cells.

252.sol: Mangroves which form shallow littoral forests near sea shores areas are halophytes. Mangrove grow in physiologically dry environment (water is available in plenty but in the form of strong salt solution). These plants develop shallow rootings due to water logged environment where oxygen scarcity prevails. To ensure proper aeration in root system, plants produce respiratory roots or pneumatophores which are negatively geotropic peg-like projections above ground with numerous pores or lenticels for gaseous exchange:

5797.subject: Chemistry
5797.text: Freundlich adsorption isotherm fails at which of the following condition?
5797.sol: The Freundlich adsorption isotherm is the mathematical representation for the variation of the extent of adsorption $(x / m)$ with pressure $(p)$ at a given temperature. x / m=k \cdot p^{1 / n}(n>1) where ' $ x$ ' is the mass of the gas adsorbed on mass ' $m$ ' of the adsorbent at pressure ' $p$ '. ' $k$ ' and ' $n$ ' are constants that depend on the nature of the adsorbent and the gas at a particular temperature. Experimentally, it was determined that the extent of gas adsorption varies with pressure raised to the power $1 / n$ until saturation pressure $p_s$ is reached. At high pressure, $x / m$ becomes independent of pressure. Hence, Freundlich equation becomes x / m=k \cdot p⁰ \Rightarrow x / m=k Thus, the Freundlich adsorption isotherm fails at higher pressure.

8768.text: Let $f: R \to R$ be a function defined by $f ( x ) = \dfrac{4x}{{4}^{x} + 2}$. what is the value of $f\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right) + 2f\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + f\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) =$?
8768.sol:
Given,& $f ( x ) = \dfrac{4x}{{4}^{x} + 2}$

We will show that for the given function~$f ( 1 - x ) = 1 - f ( x )$

$f ( 1 - x ) = \dfrac{41 - x}{{4}^{1 - x} + 2}$

$= \dfrac{4 \cdot {4}^{- x}}{4 \cdot {4}^{- x} + 2}$

$= \dfrac{4}{4 + 2 \cdot {4}^{x}}$

$= \dfrac{{4}^{x} + 2 - {4}^{x}}{2 + {4}^{x}}$

$= \dfrac{{4}^{x} + 2}{2 + {4}^{x}} - \dfrac{4x}{2 + {4}^{x}}$

$= 1 - \dfrac{4x}{2 + {4}^{x}}$

$= 1 - f ( x )$

$⇒ f \left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right) =f \left($1 - $\dfrac{3}{4}\right) =$1 - $f\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)

Now,~f\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right) +2f\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) +f\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) =$1 - f $\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) +$2f $\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + f\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)$

$= 1 + 2f $\$left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$$

$= 1 + 2 \$left[\dfrac{4\dfrac{1}{2}}{{4}^{\dfrac{1}{2}} + 2}\right]$

$= 1 + 2 $\times $\dfrac{2}{4}$

$= 2$

14521.text: Electrostatic force between two identical charges placed in vacuum at distance of $r$ is $F$. A slab of width $\dfrac{r}{5}$ and dielectric constant $9$ is inserted between these two charges, then the force between the charges is
14521.sol:
Force between the two charges when it is placed in vacuum and distance between them is $r$ is~$F = \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}}\dfrac{{q}_{1}{q}_{2}}{r2}$.

Now,~the force when a dielectric& $\left(k\right)$ is inserted between these two charges is~$F = \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}}\dfrac{{q}_{1}{q}_{2}}{kr^{' 2}}$.

On comparing the dielectric force with the vacuum force we will get,~$r^{2} = kr^{' 2}$

Or~$r^{'} = r\sqrt{k}$

Hence, the effective thickness of slab is~$\dfrac{r}{5}\sqrt{k}$.

Thus,~the force between the charges is& $F^{'} = \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}}\dfrac{{q}_{1}{q}_{2}}{\left(\dfrac{r}{5} + \dfrac{r}{5}\sqrt{9}\right)2} = \dfrac{{q}_{1}{q}_{2}}{4\pi{ε}_{0}} \times \dfrac{25}{16r^{2}} = \dfrac{25}{16}F$

16802.text: When the absolute temperature of the source of a Carnot heat engine is increased by $25 \%$, its efficiency increases by $80 \%$. The new efficiency of the engine is
16802.sol:
According to the question, initially
$\begin{aligned}
& \eta=\frac{100-T_2}{100} \\
& =\eta+\eta \times \frac{80}{100}=1.8 \eta=\frac{125-T_2}{125} \\
& \frac{\eta}{\eta^{\prime}}=\frac{100-T_2}{100} \times \frac{125}{125-T_2} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{18}=\frac{100-T_2}{100} \times \frac{125}{125-T_2} \\
& \text{ or, } \frac{5}{9}=\frac{100-T_2}{100} \times \frac{5}{\left(125-T_2\right)} \\
& \text{ or, } 9\left(100-\mathrm{T}_2\right)=500-4 \mathrm{ T}_2 \\
& \text{ or, } 900-9 \mathrm{ T}_2=500-4 \mathrm{ T}_2 \\
& \text{ or, } 400=5 \mathrm{ T}_2 \\
& \text{ or, } \mathrm{T}_2=\frac{400}{5}=80
\end{aligned}$
The new efficiency,
$\begin{aligned}
& \eta^{\prime \prime}=1-\frac{T_2}{T_1}=1-\frac{80}{125} \\
& \frac{125-80}{125}=\frac{45}{125}=\frac{45}{125} \times 100=36 \%
\end{aligned}$

19767.subject: Chemistry
19767.text:
Choose the incorrect statement from the following:
A. Isoelectronic molecules/ions have the same bond order.
B. Dipole moment of $\mathrm{NH}_3$ is greater than that of $\mathrm{NF}_3$.
C. The Carbon in Methyl Carbocation is $\mathrm{sp}^3$ hybridised.
D. The stability of an ionic compound is measured in terms of its lattice enthalpy and not simply based on attaining Octet configuration.
19767.sol:
A. Correct: Isoelectronic species like $N_2$, $CO$, $CN^-$, $NO^+$ all have bond order 3 — this holds for many common pairs.

B. Correct: In $NH_3$, N-H bond dipoles and the lone pair dipole reinforce each other. In $NF_3$, the N-F bond dipoles oppose the lone pair dipole, partially canceling it. Hence $\mu(NH_3) > \mu(NF_3)$.

C. Incorrect: The carbon in methyl carbocation ($CH_3^+$) has 3 sigma bonds and one empty p-orbital — it is $sp^2$ hybridised with trigonal planar geometry, not $sp^3$.

D. Correct: The stability of an ionic compound is governed by lattice enthalpy (energy released when gaseous ions form a crystal lattice), not merely by whether the octet rule is satisfied.

The incorrect statement is C.

19870.subject: Chemistry
19870.text: The time needed for completion of $80 \%$ is $y$ times the half-life period of a first order reaction. What is the value of $y$ ?
19870.sol:
For a first order reaction, the rate constant $k$ is given by $k = \dfrac{2.303}{t} \log \left( \dfrac{[A]_0}{[A]_t} \right).

The half-life period $t_{1/2}$ is given by $t_{1/2} = $\dfrac{0.693}{k}.

For 80\%$ completion, the amount remaining $[A]_t = [A]_0 - 0.80[A]_0 = 0.20[A]_0$.

The time taken for $80\%$ completion is $t_{80\%} = \dfrac{2.303}{k} \log \left( \dfrac{[A]_0}{0.20[A]_0} \right) = \dfrac{2.303}{k} \log(5)$.

Using $\log(5) $\approx$0.699$, we have $t_{80\%} = \dfrac{2.303 \times 0.699}{k} \approx \dfrac{1.609}{k}.

Given $ t_{80\%} = y $\times$ t_{1/2}$, we substitute the expressions:

\dfrac{1.609}{k} =$ y $\times \dfrac{0.693}{k}.

$ y = $\dfrac{1.609}{0.693} \approx2.32$.

Answer: $2.32$

Arrange the following ions in the decreasing order of total covalent double bonds formed by the transition metal(s) with oxygen.
A. = chromate B. = permanganate C. = dichromate
20065.sol:
Chromate (CrO_4^{2-}$): Cr is in +6 state, bonded to 4 oxygens. Structure has 2 double bonds (Cr=O$) and 2 single bonds (Cr-O^-$). Total $= 2$

Permanganate (MnO_4^-$): Mn is in +7 state, bonded to 4 oxygens. Structure has 3 double bonds (Mn=O$) and 1 single bond (Mn-O^-$). Total $= 3$

Dichromate (Cr_2O_7^{2-}$): Two Cr atoms linked by a bridging oxygen. Each Cr has 2 double bonds (Cr=O$). Total $= 2 \times 2 = 4$

Decreasing order: $C > B > A$ (Dichromate > Permanganate > Chromate)

20207.text: Which of the following particulate matter is emitted from vehicles?
20207.sol:
Particulate matter refers to solid or liquid particles suspended in the air. Among the given options, Lead (Pb) is a well-known heavy metal pollutant emitted from vehicle exhausts, particularly in regions where leaded gasoline was historically used or due to the wear and tear of vehicle components containing lead. Carbon monoxide (CO) is a gaseous pollutant, not particulate matter. Tin (Sn) and Selenium (Se) are not primary particulate emissions associated with standard vehicle exhaust systems.

Answer: Pb

20792.subject: Chemistry
20792.text: The energy of an electron in the ground state of Hydrogen atom is $-2.18 \times 10^{-18} \mathrm{ J}$. What would be the energy associated with the second excited state of $\mathrm{Li}$ ?
20792.sol:
The energy of an electron in a hydrogen-like species is given by the formula $E_n = -2.18 \times 10^{-18} \times \dfrac{Z^2}{n^2} \text{ J}$, where $Z$ is the atomic number and $n$ is the principal quantum number.

For Lithium (Li), the atomic number $Z = 3$.

The ground state corresponds to $n = 1$, the first excited state to $n = 2$, and the second excited state to $n = 3$.

Substituting $Z = 3$ and $n = 3$ into the formula:

$E_3 = -2.18 \times 10^{-18} \times \dfrac{3^2}{3^2} \text{ J}$

$E_3 = -2.18 \times 10^{-18} \times \dfrac{9}{9} \text{ J}$

$E_3 = -2.18 \times 10^{-18} \text{ J}$

Answer: $-2.18 \times 10^{-18} \mathrm{ J}$

20840.text:
The standard enthalpies of formation of CH$_4$(g), CO$_2$(g) and H$_2$O(l) are $-74.8$ kJ mol$^{-1}$, $-393.5$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ and $-285.8$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ respectively. Then the enthalpy change for the given reaction in kJ mol$^{-1}$ will be:
$2\text{CH}_4(g) + 4\text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2(g) + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$
20840.sol:
The enthalpy of reaction is calculated using the standard enthalpies of formation of the products and reactants.

$\Delta_{r}H^{\circ} = \sum \Delta_{f}H^{\circ}(\text{products}) - \sum \Delta_{f}H^{\circ}(\text{reactants})$

For the given reaction:

$\Delta_{r}H^{\circ} = [2 \Delta_{f}H^{\circ}(\text{CO}_{2}) + 4 \Delta_{f}H^{\circ}(\text{H}_{2}\text{O})] - [2 \Delta_{f}H^{\circ}(\text{CH}_{4}) + 4 \Delta_{f}H^{\circ}(\text{O}_{2})]$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta_{r}H^{\circ} = [2(-393.5) + 4(-285.8)] - [2(-74.8) + 4(0)]$

$\Delta_{r}H^{\circ} = [-787.0 - 1143.2] - [-149.6]$

$\Delta_{r}H^{\circ} = -1930.2 + 149.6 = -1780.6 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $-1780.6$

Let $x = 3^{\log_{4} 5} - 5^{\log_{4} 3}$.

Using the property of logarithms $a^{\log_{\mathrm{b}} c} = c^{\log_{\mathrm{b}} a}$, we compare the two terms.

Therefore, $x = 3^{\log_{4} 5} - 3^{\log_{4} 5} = 0$.

22362.subject: Physics
22362.text: In which of the following circuit do we find the current and voltage in phase?
options: A circuit in which an inductor and a capacitor are in series.
22362.sol:
In an AC circuit, the phase relationship between voltage $V$ and current $I$ depends on the nature of the components present.

For a purely capacitive circuit, the current leads the voltage by a phase angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

For a purely inductive circuit, the current lags behind the voltage by a phase angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

For a circuit containing an inductor and a capacitor in series, the phase difference depends on the values of inductive reactance $X_L$ and capacitive reactance $X_C$. The phase angle $\phi$ is given by $\tan \phi = \dfrac{X_L - X_C}{R}$. Only when $X_L = X_C$ (resonance) is the phase difference zero, but this is not true for all such circuits.

For a purely resistive circuit, the voltage and current are in phase, meaning the phase difference is $0$.

Answer: A purely resistive circuit

22948.subject: Physics
22948.text: A cubical box of side $1 \mathrm{ m}$ contains Boron gas at a pressure of $100 \mathrm{ Nm}^{-2}$. During an observation time of 1 second, an atom travelling with the rms speed parallel to one of the edges of the cube, was found to make 500 hits with a particular wall, without any collision with other atoms. The total mass of gas in the box in gram is
22948.sol:
The side length of the cubical box is $L = 1 \text{ m}$. The volume of the box is $V = L^3 = 1 \text{ m}^3$.

An atom travels with rms speed $v_{rms}$ parallel to an edge. In 1 second, it makes 500 hits on a wall. Since it travels back and forth between two opposite walls, the distance covered in one round trip is $2L = 2 \text{ m}$. The number of hits in 1 second is $N = 500$. The time taken for one round trip is $t = \dfrac{2L}{v_{rms}}$. The number of hits per second is $\dfrac{1}{t} = \dfrac{v_{rms}}{2L}$.

Given $\dfrac{v_{rms}}{2L} = 500$, we have $v_{rms} = 500 \times 2 \times 1 = 1000 \text{ m/s}$.

The pressure of an ideal gas is given by $P = \dfrac{1}{3} \rho v_{rms}^2$, where $\rho = \dfrac{M}{V}$ is the density and $M$ is the total mass of the gas.

Substituting the given values: $100 = \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{M}{1} \times (1000)^2$.

$100 = \dfrac{M \times 10^6}{3} \Rightarrow M = \dfrac{300}{10^6} = 3 \times 10^{-4} \text{ kg}$.

Converting the mass to grams: $M = 3 \times 10^{-4} \times 10^3 \text{ g} = 0.3 \text{ g}$.

Answer: 0.3

24710.text:
In a conductometric titration, small volume of titrant of higher concentration is added stepwise to a larger volume of titrate of much lower concentration, and the conductance is measured after each addition. The limiting ionic conductivity $\left(\Lambda_0\right)$ values (in $\mathrm{mS} \mathrm{m}^2 \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$) for different ions in aqueous solutions are given below:
For different combinations of titrates and titrants given in List-I, the graphs of 'conductance' versus 'volume of titrant' are given in List-II. Match each entry in List-I with the appropriate entry in List-II and choose the correct option.
24710.sol:
Option (P) :
On adding $\mathrm{AgNO}_3$ solution to $\mathrm{KCl}$ solution precipitation of $\mathrm{AgCl}$ will occur due to which $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$already present will be replaced by $\mathrm{NO}_3^{-}$ions. So conductance of solution will decrease till equivalence point. After complete precipitation of $\mathrm{AgCl}$, further added $\mathrm{AgNO}_3$ will increase the number of ions in resulting solution so conductance will increase.
Option $(\mathbf{Q})$ :
On adding $\mathrm{KCl}$ solution to $\mathrm{AgNO}_3$ solution precipitation of $\mathrm{AgCl}$ will occur due to which already present $\mathrm{Ag}^{+}$ions will be replaced by $\mathrm{K}^{+}$ions in solution. So conductance of solution will increase. After complete precipitation of $\mathrm{AgCl}$ further added $\mathrm{KCl}$ will increase the number of ions in resulting solution so conductance will increase further.
Option (R) :
On adding $\mathrm{HCl}$ solution to $\mathrm{NaOH}$ solution, $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$will be replaced by $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ions so conductance of solution decreases. After complete neutralisation further added $\mathrm{HCl}$ will increase number of ions in the solution. So conductance will increase further.
Option (S) :
On adding $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}$ solution to $\mathrm{NaOH}$ solution $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$will be replaced by $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COO}^{-}$ions, so conductance of solution decreases. After complete neutralisation further added $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}$ will remain undissociated because it is a weak acid and there is also common ion effect on acetate ions. So number of ions in solution will remain almost constant therefore conductance of solution will remain constant.

28040.subject: Chemistry
28040.text: The following concentrations were observed at $500K$ for the formation of ${NH}_{3}$ from ${N}_{2} and {H}_{2}$. At equilibrium : $\left[{N}_{2}\right] = 2 \times {10}^{- 2}M, \left[{H}_{2}\right] = 3 \times {10}^{- 2}M$ and $\left[{NH}_{3}\right] = 1 . 5 \times {10}^{- 2}M$. Equilibrium constant for the reaction is ______.
28040.sol:
The equilibrium constant of concentration (denoted by ${K}_{c}$) of a chemical reaction at equilibrium can be defined as the ratio of the concentration of products to the concentration of the reactants, each raised to their respective stoichiometric coefficients.

The equilibrium reaction is 

${N}_{2\left(g\right)} + 3{H}_{2\left(g\right)}\mathop{⇋}_{}^{}2{NH}_{3\left(g\right)}$

${K}_{c} = \dfrac{{\left[{NH}_{3}\right]}^{2}}{{\left[{H}_{2}\right]}^{3}\left[{N}_{2}\right]}$

$E_{a1} - E_{a2} = 20$ kJ/mol = 20000 J/mol
$\frac{k_2}{k_1} = e^{\frac{20000}{8.3 \times 300}} = e^{\frac{20000}{2490}}$
$\ln\frac{k_2}{k_1} = \frac{20000}{2490} = 8.03 \approx 8$

The boiling point of organic compounds depends on two factors:

32956.text:
Let a function $f: \left[0, 5\right] \to R$ be continuous, $f\left(1\right) = 3$ and $F$ be defined as:
$F\left(x\right) = {∫}_{1}^{x}{t}^{2}g\left(t\right)dt,$ where $g\left(t\right) = {∫}_{1}^{t}f\left(u\right)du .$

Then for the function $F\left(x\right),$ the point $x = 1$ is:
32956.sol:
Given, $F\left(x\right) = {∫}_{1}^{x}{t}^{2}g\left(t\right)dt$

By Leibnitz rule we get,

${F}^{'}\left(x\right) = {x}^{2}g\left(x\right)$

$⇒ {F}^{'}\left(1\right) = 1 . g\left(1\right) = 0$ $\left(∵ g\left(1\right) = 0\right)$

Now ${F}^{''}\left(x\right) = 2xg\left(x\right) + {x}^{2}{g}^{'}\left(x\right)$

$⇒ {F}^{''}\left(x\right) = 2xg\left(x\right) + {x}^{2}f\left(x\right)$ $\left(∵ {g}^{'}\left(x\right) = f\left(x\right)\right)$

$⇒ {F}^{''}\left(1\right) = 0 + 1 \times 3$

$⇒ {F}^{''}\left(1\right) = 3$

$F\left(x\right)$ has a local minimum at $x = 1$.

The equation of the tangent to ${y}^{2} = 4x$ is $y = mx + \dfrac{a}{m}$
The equation of the tangent to ${x}^{2} = 4by$ is $y = mx - b{m}^{2}$

Since, they have a common tangent,

$\dfrac{a}{m} = - b{m}^{2}$

$∴ \dfrac{1}{m} = 8{m}^{2}$

$∴ {m}^{3} = \dfrac{1}{8}$

$∴ m = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$∴$ The slope of the common tangent is $\dfrac{1}{2}$.

33209.text: The area (in sq. units) of the region $A = \left\{\left(x, y\right): {x}^{2} \le y \le x + 2\right\}$ is
33209.sol:
The two given curves are $y = x + 2$ and $y = {x}^{2}$

To find their points of intersection, we equate the value of $y$ to get

${x}^{2} = x + 2$

$⇒ {x}^{2} - x - 2 = 0$

$⇒ \left(x - 2\right)\left(x + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ x = 2$ or $x = - 1 .$

The graphs of the curves are given below.


Required area is the area of the shaded portion.

Area $= {∫}_{- 1}^{2}\left({y}_{line} - {y}_{parabola}\right)dx$
$= {∫}_{- 1}^{2}\left(x + 2 - {x}^{2}\right)dx$

Using $∫ {x}^{n}dx = \dfrac{{x}^{n + 1}}{n + 1}$

$= {\left[\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} + 2x - \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3}\right]}_{- 1}^{2}$

$= \left(2 + 4 - \dfrac{8}{3}\right) - \left(\dfrac{1}{2} - 2 + \dfrac{1}{3}\right)$

$= 6 - \dfrac{8}{3} - \dfrac{1}{2} + 2 - \dfrac{1}{3}$

$= 8 - 3 - \dfrac{1}{2}$

$= \dfrac{9}{2}$ sq units.

33381.text:
The constant term in the expansion of
${\left(2x + \dfrac{1}{{x}^{7}} + 3{x}^{2}\right)}^{5}$ is _____ .
33381.sol:
Any term in the expansion of ${\left(2x + \dfrac{1}{{x}^{7}} + 3{x}^{2}\right)}^{5}$ is given by

$\dfrac{5 !}{a ! \cdot b ! \cdot c !}{\left(2x\right)}^{a}{\left({x}^{- 7}\right)}^{b}{\left(3{x}^{2}\right)}^{c}$

where $a + b + c = 5 . . . \left(i\right)$

$= {2}^{a}{\left(3\right)}^{c}\left(\dfrac{5 !}{a ! \cdot b ! \cdot c !}\right){x}^{a}{x}^{- 7b}{x}^{2c}$

$= {2}^{a}{\left(3\right)}^{c}\left(\dfrac{5 !}{a ! \cdot b ! \cdot c !}\right){x}^{a - 7b + 2c}$

Now for term to be independent of $x$, we know

$a - 7b + 2c = 0 . . . \left(ii\right)$

Solving $\left(i\right) \text{$ and }$\left(ii\right), we get

$b = $\dfrac{c + 5}{8}

Also, $a, b, c \in $\left\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\right\}$

So, $a = 1, b = 1, c = 3$

Therefore, the term independent of $x$ will be

${2}^{1}{\left(3\right)}^{3} \cdot \dfrac{5 !}{1 ! \cdot 1 ! \cdot 3 !} = 1080$

34845.text: The curve satisfying the differential equation, $\left(x^2-y^2\right) d x+2 x y d y=0$ and passing through the point $(1,1)$ is
options:
a circle of radius two

a circle of radius one

a hyperbola

an ellipse
34845.sol:
$\left(x^2-y^2\right) d x+2 x y d y=0 ⇒ \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{y^2-x^2}{2 x y}$Let $y=v x \begin{aligned}$& $\frac{d y}{d x}=$v+x $\frac{d v}{d x}$\\
\Rightarrow & v+x $\frac{d v}{d x}=\frac{v^2 x^2-x^2}{2 v x^2}$\\
\Rightarrow & v+x $\frac{d v}{d x}=\frac{v^2-1}{2 v}$\\
\Rightarrow & x $\frac{d v}{d x}=\frac{-v^2-1}{2 v}$\\
\Rightarrow & $\frac{2 v d v}{v^2+1}=-\frac{d x}{x}
\end{aligned}$After integrating, we get

$\begin{aligned}$&\ln $\left|$v^2+1\right|=-\ln |x|+\ln c \\
&$\frac{y^2}{x^2}+$1=$\frac{c}{x}
\end{aligned}$As curve passes through the point $(1,1)$, so $1+1=c \Rightarrow c=2x^2+y^2-2 x=0$, which is a circle of radius one.

By applying integration by parts $\begin{aligned} & I=-\cot x \operatorname{cosec}^3 x+\int \cot x\left(-3 \operatorname{cosec}^2 x \cot x \operatorname{cosec} x\right) d x \\ & I=-\cot x \operatorname{cosec}^3 x-3 \int \operatorname{cosec}^3 x\left(\operatorname{cosec}^2 x-1\right) d x \\ & I=-\cot x \operatorname{cosec}^3 x-3 I+3 \int \operatorname{cosec}^3 x d x \end{aligned}$ let $\begin{aligned} & I_1=\int \operatorname{cosec}^3 x d x=-\operatorname{cosec} x \cot x-\int \cot ^2 x \operatorname{cosec} x d x \\ & I_1=-\operatorname{cosec} x \cot x-\int\left(\operatorname{cosec}^2 x-1\right) \operatorname{cosec} x d x \end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & 2 I_1=-\operatorname{cosec} x \cot x+\ln \left|\tan \frac{x}{2}\right| \\ & I_1=-\frac{1}{2} \operatorname{cosec} x \cot x+\frac{1}{2} \ln \left|\tan \frac{x}{2}\right| \\ & 4 I=-\cot x \operatorname{cosec}^3 x-\frac{3}{2} \operatorname{cosec} x \cot x+\frac{3}{2} \ln \left|\tan \frac{x}{2}\right|+4 c \\ & I=-\frac{1}{4} \operatorname{cosec} x \cot x\left(\operatorname{cosec}^2 x+\frac{3}{2}\right)+\frac{3}{8} \ln \left|\tan \frac{x}{2}\right|+c \\ & \therefore \alpha=\frac{-1}{4}, \beta=\frac{3}{8} \rightarrow 8(\alpha+\beta)=1\end{aligned}$

35500.text: Let $I\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{x + 1}{x{\left(1 + x{e}^{x}\right)}^{2}}dx, x > 0 .$ If $\lim_{x \to \infty}I\left(x\right) = 0$ then $I\left(1\right)$ is equal to
35500.sol:
Given,

$I\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{x + 1}{x{\left(1 + x{e}^{x}\right)}^{2}}dx$

Now let $1 + x{e}^{x} = t$

$⇒ {e}^{x}\left(x + 1\right)dx = dt$

So, $I\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{1}{\left(t - 1\right){t}^{2}}dt$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{\left(1 - {t}^{2}\right) + {t}^{2}}{\left(t - 1\right){t}^{2}}dt$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{- \left(t + 1\right)}{{t}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{t - 1}dt$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = ∫ - \dfrac{1}{t} - \dfrac{1}{{t}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{t - 1}dt$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = - lnt + \dfrac{1}{t} + ln\left(t - 1\right) + C$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = ln\left(\dfrac{x{e}^{x}}{x{e}^{x} + 1}\right) + \dfrac{1}{x{e}^{x} + 1} + C$

Also given,$\lim_{x \to \infty}I\left(x\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to \infty}I\left(x\right) = \lim_{x \to \infty}\left[ln\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{x{e}^{x} + 1}\right) + \dfrac{1}{x{e}^{x} + 1} + C\right]$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to \infty}I\left(x\right) = \left[ln\left(1 - 0\right) + 0 + C\right]$

$⇒ C = 0$

Now finding,

$I\left(1\right) = ln\left(\dfrac{e}{e + 1}\right) + \dfrac{1}{e + 1} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{e + 1} - ln ( e + 1 )$

$⇒ I\left(1\right) = \dfrac{e + 2}{e + 1} - ln\left(e + 1\right)$

35509.text: If $∫ \dfrac{sinx}{\sin^{3}x + \cos^{3}x}dx = \alpha{\log}_{e} | 1 + tanx | + \beta{\log}_{e}\left|1 - tanx + \tan^{2}x\right| + \gamma\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2tanx - 1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + C,$ when $C$ is constant of integration, then the value of $18\left(\alpha + \beta + {\gamma}^{2}\right)$ is
35509.sol:
$∫ \dfrac{sinx}{\sin^{3}x + \cos^{3}x}dx = \alpha{\log}_{e} | 1 + tanx | + \beta{\log}_{e}\left|1 - tanx + \tan^{2}x\right| + \gamma\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2tanx - 1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + C, . . . . . . . . . . \left(i\right)$

Let, $I = ∫ \dfrac{sinx}{\sin^{3}x + \cos^{3}x}dx$
$I = ∫ \dfrac{tanx{sec}^{2}x}{\tan^{3} + 1}dx$

Put $tanx = t ⇒ {sec}^{2}xdx = dt$

$= ∫ \dfrac{tdt}{{t}^{3} + 1} = ∫ \dfrac{t}{( t + 1 ) \left({t}^{2} - t + 1\right)}dt$
Now $\dfrac{t}{( t + 1 ) \left({t}^{2} - t + 1\right)} = \dfrac{A}{t + 1} + \dfrac{Bt + C}{{t}^{2} - t + 1}$

$t = A\left({t}^{2} - t + 1\right) + ( Bt + C ) ( t + 1 )$

$t = {t}^{2}\left(A + B\right) - t\left(A - B - C\right) + A + C$

Comparing on both sides

$A + B = 0, - A + B + C = 1, A + C = 0$

Solving these equations
$A = - \dfrac{1}{3}, B = \dfrac{1}{3}, C = \dfrac{1}{3}$

36216.text: Let $P ( \alpha, \beta )$ be a point on the parabola ${y}^{2} = 4x$. If $P$ also lies on the chord of the parabola ${x}^{2} = 8y$ whose mid point is $\left(1, \dfrac{5}{4}\right)$, then $( \alpha - 28 ) ( \beta - 8 )$ is equal to _______.
36216.sol:
Given,

Parabola ${x}^{2} = 8y$

We know that,

Chord with mid point $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right)$ is $T = {S}_{1}$

$x{x}_{1} - 8\left(\dfrac{y + {y}_{1}}{2}\right) = {x}_{1} - 2 8{y}_{1}$

$⇒ x{x}_{1} - 4\left(y + {y}_{1}\right) = {x}_{1} - 2 8{y}_{1}$

Now, putting the point $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right) = \left(1, \dfrac{5}{4}\right)$ we get,

$⇒ x - 4\left(y + \dfrac{5}{4}\right) = 1 - 8 \times \dfrac{5}{4} = - 9$

$∴ x - 4y + 4 = 0 \ldots \left(i\right)$

$( \alpha, \beta )$ lies on (i) and also on ${y}^{2} = 4x$

$∴ \alpha - 4\beta + 4 = 0 \ldots \left(ii\right)

And ${\beta}^{2} = 4\alpha \ldots $\left(iii\right)$

Solving (ii) and (iii)

${\beta}^{2} = 4 ( 4\beta - 4 )$

$⇒ {\beta}^{2} - 16\beta + 16 = 0$

$⇒ \beta = 8 \pm 4\sqrt{3}$ 

And $\alpha = 4\beta - 4 = 28 \pm 16\sqrt{3}$

$∴ \left(\alpha, \beta\right) = \left(28 + 16\sqrt{3}, 8 + 4\sqrt{3}\right)$ and ( 28 - 16\sqrt{3}, 8 - 4\sqrt{3} )$

Now, solving

$( \alpha - 28 ) ( \beta - 8 ) = ( 16\sqrt{3} ) ( 4\sqrt{3} )$

$⇒ ( \alpha - 28 ) ( \beta - 8 ) = 192$

$

38125.text: Let $L$ be the line of intersection of planes $\overset{\to}{r} \cdot ( \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k} ) = 2$ and $\overset{\to}{r} \cdot ( 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k} ) = 2 .$ If $P ( \alpha, \beta, \gamma )$ is the foot of perpendicular on $L$ from the point $( 1, 2, 0 ) ,$ then the value of $35 ( \alpha + \beta + \gamma )$ is equal to:
38125.sol:
The given planes are $\overset{\to}{r} \cdot ( \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k} ) = 2$ and $\overset{\to}{r} \cdot ( 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k} ) = 2 .$

We can convert these planes into cartesian form by taking $\overset{\to}{r} = x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j} + z\overset{^}{k}$

Thus, we have $\left(x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j} + z\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot ( \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k} ) = 2$ and $\left(x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j} + z\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot ( 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k} ) = 2$

$⇒ x - y + 2z = 2$ and $2x + y - z = 2$

So, let ${P}_{1} ≡ x - y + 2z = 2$ and ${P}_{2} ≡ 2x + y - z = 2$

Let, the line of Intersection $L$ of planes ${P}_{1}$ and ${P}_{2}$ cuts $xy$ plane in point $Q$ and it is given that the foot of perpendicular $P$ on $L$ from a point $F$ is $F\left(1, 2, 0\right),$ and this point is also on the $xy$ plane.

From the diagram it is clear that, $PQ$ is a line in the $xy$ plane and hence at every point on it the $z$-coordinate is zero.

$⇒ z$-coordinate of point $Q,$ is zero and it is on both the planes,

$⇒ x - y = 2 . . . \left(i\right)$

And, $2x + y = 2 . . . \left(ii\right)$

On solving the above two equation, we get $x = \dfrac{4}{3}, y = \dfrac{- 2}{3} .$

$⇒ Q\left(\dfrac{4}{3}, - \dfrac{2}{3}, 0\right)$

A vector parallel to the line of intersection can be obtained by finding a vector which is perpendicular to both the planes.

And, we know that a vector perpendicular to two vectors can be obtained by finding their cross product, i.e. the vector parallel to the line of intersection is

$\overset{\to}{a} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & - 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & - 1\end{cases}\right| = - \overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

Now, we know that the equation of a line passing through a point $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right)$ and parallel to a vector $a\overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + c\overset{^}{k}$ is $\dfrac{x - {x}_{1}}{a} = \dfrac{y - {y}_{1}}{b} = \dfrac{z - {z}_{1}}{c} .$

Thus, the equation of the line of intersection of the planes is

$\dfrac{x - \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)}{\left(- 1\right)} = \dfrac{y + \dfrac{2}{3}}{5} = \dfrac{z - 0}{3}$

$\dfrac{x - \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)}{\left(- 1\right)} = \dfrac{y + \dfrac{2}{3}}{5} = \dfrac{z}{3} = \lambda$ $($let$)$

$⇒ x = - \lambda + \dfrac{4}{3}, y = 5\lambda - \dfrac{2}{3} \text{ and } z = 3\lambda .$

Let, coordinates of foot of perpendicular be

$P ≡ \left(- \lambda + \dfrac{4}{3}, 5\lambda - \dfrac{2}{3}, 3\lambda\right)$

Now, $\overset{\to}{PF} = \left(- \lambda + \dfrac{4}{3} - 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(5\lambda - \dfrac{2}{3} - 2\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(3\lambda - 0\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{PF} = \left(- \lambda + \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(5\lambda - \dfrac{8}{3}\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(3\lambda\right)\overset{^}{k}$

Now, since $\overset{\to}{PF}$ is perpendicular to the line, hence the dot product of their direction ratios is zero.

$⇒ \left(- 1\right)\left(- \lambda + \dfrac{1}{3}\right) + 5\left(5\lambda - \dfrac{8}{3}\right) + 3\left(3\lambda\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda - \dfrac{1}{3} + 25\lambda - \dfrac{40}{3} + 9\lambda = 0$

$⇒ 35\lambda = \dfrac{41}{3}$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{41}{105} .$

Now, $\alpha = - \lambda + \dfrac{4}{3}, \beta = 5\lambda - \dfrac{2}{3}, \gamma = 3\lambda$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta + \gamma = 7\lambda + \dfrac{2}{3}$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta + \gamma = 7\left(\dfrac{41}{105}\right) + \dfrac{2}{3}$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta + \gamma = \dfrac{51}{15}$

$⇒ 35 ( \alpha + \beta + \gamma ) = \dfrac{51}{15} \times 35 = 119 .$

38167.sol:
Lines $\overset{\to}{r} = \left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}\right) + l\left(2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$ and $\overset{\to}{r} = \left(2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}\right) + m\left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right)$

Clearly both lines do not have same direction means lines are not parallel.

$⇒$Lines are skew lines or intersecting lines.

Let lines are skew lines and distance between lines is $d$ if distance between them comes out zero then they will be intersecting lines.

For lines $\overset{\to}{r} = \overset{\to}{a} + \lambda\overset{\to}{p}, \overset{\to}{r} = \overset{\to}{b} + \lambda\overset{\to}{q}$

$d = \dfrac{\left(\overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{a}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{p} \times \overset{\to}{q}\right)}{\left|\overset{\to}{p} \times \overset{\to}{q}\right|}$

Applying here

$d = \dfrac{\left(2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} - \left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}\right)\right) \cdot \left(\left(2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right) \times \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right)\right)}{\left|\left(2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right) \times \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right)\right|}$

$d = \dfrac{\left(\overset{^}{i}\right) \cdot \left(- \overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)}{\left|- \overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right|} = \left|- \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{14}}\right| = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{14}}$

$⇒$Lines are skew lines means do not intersect.

38322.text: Let $S = \left\{\theta \in ( 0, 2\pi ) : 7\cos^{2}\theta - 3\sin^{2}\theta - 2\cos^{2}2\theta = 2\right\}$. Then, the sum of roots of all the equations ${x}^{2} - 2\left(\tan^{2}\theta + {cot}^{2}\theta\right)x + 6\sin^{2}\theta = 0\theta \in S$, is _______.
38322.sol:
Given,

$7\cos^{2}\theta - 3\sin^{2}\theta - 2\cos^{2}2\theta = 2$

$⇒ 7\cos^{2}\theta - 3\left(1 - \cos^{2}\theta\right) - 2\cos^{2}2\theta = 2$

$⇒ 4\cos^{2}\theta + 3cos2\theta - 2\cos^{2}2\theta = 2$

$⇒ 2\left(1 + cos2\theta\right) + 3cos2\theta - 2\cos^{2}2\theta = 2$

$⇒ 2\cos^{2}2\theta - 5cos2\theta = 0$

$⇒ cos2\theta\left(2cos2\theta - 5\right) = 0$

$⇒ cos2\theta = 0$ or $2cos2\theta - 5 = 0\left\{\text{which is not possible}\right\}$

$⇒ 2\theta = \left(2n + 1\right)\dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$⇒ \theta = \left(2n + 1\right)\dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$S = \left\{\dfrac{\pi}{4}, \dfrac{3\pi}{4}, \dfrac{5\pi}{4}, \dfrac{7\pi}{4}\right\}$

For all four values of $\theta$, $\tan^{2}\theta \text{ and } co{\text{t}}^{2}\theta\text{will become}1\text{and}\sin^{2}\theta\text{will become}\dfrac{1}{2}$

So, ${x}^{2} - 2\left(\tan^{2}\theta + {cot}^{2}\theta\right)x + 6\sin^{2}\theta = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} - 4x + 3 = 0$

Sum of roots of all four equations $= 4 \times 4 = 16$.

38438.text: Let $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b} = 6\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$. Then the square of the area of the triangle with adjacent sides determined by the vectors $(2\vec{a} + 3\vec{b})$ and $(\vec{a} - \vec{b})$ is :
38438.sol:
The area of a triangle with adjacent sides $\vec{u}$ and $\vec{v}$ is given by $\Delta = \dfrac{1}{2} |\vec{u} \times \vec{v}|$.

Here, $\vec{u} = 2\vec{a} + 3\vec{b}$ and $\vec{v} = \vec{a} - \vec{b}$.

$\vec{u} \times \vec{v} = (2\vec{a} + 3\vec{b}) \times (\vec{a} - \vec{b})$

$\vec{u} \times \vec{v} = 2(\vec{a} \times \vec{a}) - 2(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) + 3(\vec{b} \times \vec{a}) - 3(\vec{b} \times \vec{b})$

Since $\vec{a} \times \vec{a} = \vec{0}$, $\vec{b} \times \vec{b} = \vec{0}$, and $\vec{b} \times \vec{a} = -\vec{a} \times \vec{b}$, we get:

$\vec{u} \times \vec{v} = -2(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) - 3(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) = -5(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$

The area of the triangle is $\Delta = \dfrac{1}{2} |-5(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})| = \dfrac{5}{2} |\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|$.

Now, calculating $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}$:

$\vec{a} \times \vec{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & 3 & 3 \\ 6 & 3 & 3 \end{vmatrix}$

$\vec{a} \times \vec{b} = \hat{i}(9 - 9) - \hat{j}(6 - 18) + \hat{k}(6 - 18) = 12\hat{j} - 12\hat{k}$

The square of the magnitude is:

$|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|^2 = 12^2 + (-12)^2 = 144 + 144 = 288$

The square of the area of the triangle is:

$\Delta^2 = \left( \dfrac{5}{2} \right)^2 |\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|^2 = \dfrac{25}{4} \times 288 = 25 \times 72 = 1800$

Answer: $1800$

40791.text: The resistance of the meter bridge AB in given figure is $4 \Omega$. With a cell of emf $\varepsilon=0.5 \mathrm{~V}$ and rheostat resistance $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{h}}=2 \Omega$ the null point is obtained at some point J. When the cell is replaced by another one of emf $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_{2}$ the same null point $\mathrm{J}$ is found for $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{h}}=6 \Omega$. The $\operatorname{emf} \varepsilon_{2}$ is:
40791.sol:
Given, Emf of cell, $\varepsilon=0.5 \mathrm{v}$ Rheostat resistance, $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{h}}=2 \Omega$ Potential gradient is

$\frac{d v}{d L}=\left(\frac{6}{2+4}\right) \times \frac{4}{L}$

Let null point be at $\ell \mathrm{cm}$ when cell of $\mathrm{emf} \varepsilon=0.5 \mathrm{v}$ is used.

thus $\varepsilon_{1}=0.5 \mathrm{~V}=\left(\frac{6}{2+4}\right) \times \frac{4}{\mathrm{~L}} \times \ell$...(i)

For resistance $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{h}}=6 \Omega$ new potential gradient is $\left(\frac{6}{4+6}\right) \times \frac{4}{L}$ and at null point

$\left(\frac{6}{4+6}\right)\left(\frac{4}{\mathrm{~L}}\right) \times \ell=\varepsilon_{2}$...(ii)

Dividing equation (i) by (ii) we get

$\frac{0.5}{\varepsilon_{2}}=\frac{10}{6}$ thus $\varepsilon_{2}=0.3 \mathrm{v}$

40874.subject: Physics
40874.text: For a body projected at an angle with the horizontal from the ground, choose the correct statement
options: Gravitational potential energy is maximum at the highest point.
The horizontal component of velocity is zero at highest point.
The vertical component of momentum is maximum at the highest point.
The kinetic energy (K.E.) is zero at the highest point of projectile motion.
40874.sol:
In a projectile motion, a particle has two components of velocity. The horizontal component of velocity remains constant over time, while the vertical component of velocity changes.

At highest point, the vertical component of velocity $\left({v}_{y}\right)$ becomes zero, but the horizontal component is non-zero. So the kinetic energy of the particle is not zero.

The formula to calculate the potential energy $\left(U\right)$ of the particle is given by

$U = mgh . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

where, $m$ is the mass, $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity and $h$ is the vertical height attained by the object.

Hence, the potential energy is maximum when the projectile attains the maximum height.

42257.text: The velocity of the bullet becomes one third after it penetrates $4cm$ in a wooden block. Assuming that bullet is facing a constant resistance during its motion in the block. The bullet stops completely after travelling at $\left(4 + x\right)cm$ inside the block. The value of $x$ is
42257.sol:
According to the given information for the first $4cm$, $u = {v}_{0}$ and $v = \dfrac{{v}_{0}}{3}$. Applying equation of motion for constant acceleration,

${v}^{2} = {u}^{2} + 2as$

$⇒ {\left(\dfrac{{v}_{0}}{3}\right)}^{2} = {v}^{2} + 2a\left(4\right) ⇒ a = - \dfrac{8{{v}_{0}}^{2}}{9\left(8\right)} = - \dfrac{{{v}_{0}}^{2}}{9}$

When the body stops, $v = 0$

$⇒ 0 = {{v}_{0}}^{2} + 2a\left(4 + x\right)$

$⇒ {{v}_{0}}^{2} = 2\left(\dfrac{{{v}_{0}}^{2}}{9}\right)\left(4 + x\right)$

$⇒ 4 . 5 = 4 + x$

$⇒ x = 0 . 5cm$

47646.subject: Chemistry
47646.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
47646.text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Element-Atomic number)List-II (Position in periodic table)
(a)Ra – 88(i)$4^{th}$ period, $13^{th}$ group
(b)Ga – 31(ii)$6^{th}$ period, $6^{th}$ group
(c)W – 74(iii)$5^{th}$ period, $10^{th}$ group
(d)Pd – 46(iv)$7^{th}$ period, $2^{nd}$ group
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
47646.sol:
The position of an element in the periodic table can be determined using its atomic number and the nearest preceding noble gas.

(a) Ra (Z = 88$): The preceding noble gas is Radon (Rn, $Z = 86$), which belongs to the 6^{th}$ period and $18^{th}$ group. The next two electrons enter the $7s$ orbital. Thus, Ra belongs to the $7^{th}$ period and $2^{nd}$ group. (a) \rightarrow (iv)

(b) Ga (Z = 31$): The preceding noble gas is Argon (Ar, $Z = 18$), which belongs to the 3^{rd}$ period. The next electrons fill the $4s$, $3d$, and $4p$ orbitals. The group number is $31 - 18 = 13$. Thus, Ga belongs to the $4^{th}$ period and $13^{th}$ group. (b) \rightarrow (i)

(c) W (Z = 74$): The preceding noble gas is Xenon (Xe, $Z = 54$), which belongs to the 5^{th}$ period. The next electrons fill the $6s$, $4f$ (14 elements), and $5d$ orbitals. The group number is $74 - 54 - 14 = 6$. Thus, W belongs to the $6^{th}$ period and $6^{th}$ group. (c) \rightarrow (ii)

(d) Pd (Z = 46$): The preceding noble gas is Krypton (Kr, $Z = 36$), which belongs to the 4^{th}$ period. The next electrons fill the $5s$ and $4d$ orbitals. The group number is $46 - 36 = 10$. Thus, Pd belongs to the $5^{th}$ period and $10^{th}$ group. (d) \rightarrow (iii)

The correct matching is a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.

Answer: a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d–iii

49502.text: The area of the triangle with vertices $(3, 8), (-4, 2)$ and $(5, 1)$ is $\dfrac{P}{4}$, then the value of $P$ is

The area of a triangle with vertices $(x_1, y_1)$, $(x_2, y_2)$, and $(x_3, y_3)$ is given by $\dfrac{1}{2} |x_1(y_2 - y_3) + x_2(y_3 - y_1) + x_3(y_1 - y_2)|$.

Substituting the given vertices $(3, 8)$, $(-4, 2)$, and $(5, 1)$:

Area $= \dfrac{1}{2} |3(2 - 1) - 4(1 - 8) + 5(8 - 2)|$

Area $= \dfrac{1}{2} |3(1) - 4(-7) + 5(6)|$

Area $= \dfrac{1}{2} |3 + 28 + 30| = \dfrac{61}{2}$

Given that the area is $\dfrac{P}{4}$:

$\dfrac{P}{4} = \dfrac{61}{2}$

$P = 122$

Answer: $122$

50195.text: In ruby laser, the stimulated emission is due to transition from
options: metastable state to any lower state
any higher state to lower state
any higher state to ground state
50195.sol: For a ruby laser, a crystal of ruby is formed into a cylinder. A fully reflecting mirror is placed on one end and a partially reflecting mirror on the other. A high-intensity lamp is spiraled around the ruby cylinder to provide a flash of white light that triggers the laser action. The green and blue wavelengths in the flash excite electrons in the chromium atoms to a higher energy level. Upon returning to their normal state, the electrons emit their characteristic ruby-red light. The mirrors reflect some of this light back and forth inside the ruby crystal, stimulating other excited chromium atoms to produce more red light, until the light pulse builds up to high power and drains the energy stored in the crystal. In ruby laser stimulated emission is due to transition from metastable state to ground state.

54834.subject: Chemistry
54834.text: Which among the following compounds has highest solubility in water?
54834.sol:
Solubility of organic compounds in water depends on their ability to form hydrogen bonds with water molecules, the size of the hydrophobic part, and the lattice energy of the solid.

1. Phenol forms strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds with water, making it quite soluble (solubility $\approx 8.3 \text{ g/100 mL}$).

2. p-Cresol contains an additional hydrophobic methyl ($-CH_3$) group, which increases the non-polar character and decreases its solubility compared to phenol (solubility $\approx 1.9 \text{ g/100 mL}$).

3. o-Nitrophenol exhibits intramolecular hydrogen bonding (chelation). This restricts its ability to form intermolecular hydrogen bonds with water, resulting in very low solubility (solubility $\approx 0.2 \text{ g/100 mL}$).

4. p-Nitrophenol can form intermolecular hydrogen bonds with water. However, due to its higher molecular mass and strong intermolecular interactions in the solid state (high lattice energy), its solubility is lower than that of phenol (solubility $\approx 1.6 \text{ g/100 mL}$).

Therefore, phenol has the highest solubility in water among the given compounds.

Answer: Phenol

55258.subject: Chemistry
55258.text: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: Primary amines show intermolecular hydrogen bonds.
Tertiary butylamine is a primary amine.
Tertiary amines do not show inter molecular hydrogen bonds.
55258.sol:
Primary amines have the general formula $R-NH_2$. Since they have two hydrogen atoms attached to the highly electronegative nitrogen atom, they can form intermolecular hydrogen bonds.

Tertiary butylamine has the structure $(CH_3)_3C-NH_2$. The nitrogen atom is attached to only one carbon atom, making it a primary amine.

Tertiary amines have the general formula $R_3N$. They do not have any hydrogen atoms attached to the nitrogen atom, so they cannot form intermolecular hydrogen bonds with each other.

iso-propylamine has the structure $(CH_3)_2CH-NH_2$. The nitrogen atom is attached to only one carbon atom. Therefore, it is a primary amine, not a secondary amine. The classification of amines depends on the number of alkyl groups attached to the nitrogen atom, not the degree of the carbon atom it is attached to.

Answer: iso-propylamine is a secondary amine.

55778.text: Which from following molecules is square pyramidal?
55778.sol:
Molecular geometry determination using VSEPR theory:

For $\mathrm{XeF}_4$, xenon has four bonding pairs and two lone pairs, giving octahedral electron geometry and square planar molecular geometry.

For $\mathrm{XeF}_6$, xenon has six bonding pairs and one lone pair, resulting in pentagonal bipyramidal electron geometry and distorted octahedral molecular geometry.

For $\mathrm{XeOF}_4$, xenon has five bonding domains (four single bonds to fluorine and one double bond to oxygen) and one lone pair, yielding octahedral electron geometry and square pyramidal molecular geometry.

For $\mathrm{XeO}_3$, xenon has three bonding domains (double bonds to oxygen) and one lone pair, giving tetrahedral electron geometry and trigonal pyramidal molecular geometry.

The molecule with square pyramidal geometry is $\mathrm{XeOF}_4$.

55950.subject: Chemistry
55950.text: Identify from following salts so that the solubility of salt in water decreases with increase in temperature.
55950.sol:
Most ionic compounds exhibit increased solubility in water with rising temperature due to the endothermic nature of their dissolution process. Applying Le Chatelier's principle, increasing temperature shifts the equilibrium toward the dissolved ions, enhancing solubility.

Exceptions occur when dissolution is exothermic. For these salts, elevated temperature shifts equilibrium toward the solid form, reducing solubility.

Sodium bromide and sodium chloride solubility increases with temperature, while sodium nitrate shows significant temperature-dependent solubility enhancement.

Sodium sulfate displays unique behavior: below 32.38& °C, its decahydrate form solubility increases with temperature, but above this transition point, the dissolution of anhydrous $\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{SO}_4$ becomes exothermic, causing solubility to decrease with increasing temperature.

Final Answer: $\boxed{\text{D}}$

58026.subject: Chemistry
58026.text: The solubility of sparingly soluble salt $\mathrm{AX}_2$ is $1 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{ mol } \mathrm{dm}^{-3}$ at 298 K. Calculate its solubility product?
58026.sol:
The sparingly soluble salt $\mathrm{AX}_2$ dissociates according to: $\mathrm{AX}_2(s) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{A}^{2+}(aq) + 2\mathrm{X}^{-}(aq)$
For a solubility of $s = 1 \times 10^{-4}~\mathrm{mol~dm^{-3}}$, the ion concentrations are $\left[\mathrm{A}^{2+}\right] = s and \left[\mathrm{X}^{-}\right] = 2s$

The solubility product is given by $K_{sp} = \left[\mathrm{A}^{2+}\right]\left[\mathrm{X}^{-}\right]^2$

Substituting yields $K_{sp} = (s)(2s)^2 = 4s^3$
With $s = 1 \times 10^{-4}$, we obtain $K_{sp} = 4 \times (1 \times 10^{-4})^3 = 4 \times 10^{-12}$

Final answer: $\boxed{\mathrm{B}}$

61043.text: If $\int_{2}^{e}\left[\dfrac{1}{\log x} - \dfrac{1}{(\log x)^2}\right] dx = a + \dfrac{b}{\log 2}$, then values of $a$ and $b$ are
61043.sol:
Let $I = \int_{2}^{e}\left[\dfrac{1}{\log x} - \dfrac{1}{(\log x)^2}\right] dx$

Using integration by parts on the first term:

$\int \dfrac{1}{\log x} dx = \dfrac{x}{\log x} - \int x \left( -\dfrac{1}{(\log x)^2} \right) \dfrac{1}{x} dx = \dfrac{x}{\log x} + \int \dfrac{1}{(\log x)^2} dx$

Therefore, $\int \left[ \dfrac{1}{\log x} - \dfrac{1}{(\log x)^2} \right] dx = \dfrac{x}{\log x}$

Evaluating the definite integral from $2$ to $e$:

$I = \left[ \dfrac{x}{\log x} \right]_{2}^{e} = \dfrac{e}{\log e} - \dfrac{2}{\log 2} = e - \dfrac{2}{\log 2}$

Comparing this with $a + \dfrac{b}{\log 2}$, we get $a = e$ and $b = -2$.

Answer: $a = e, b = -2$

61966.text: If the line $3x + 4y + k = 0$ touches the ellipse $9x^2 + 16y^2 = 144$, then the value of k is.
61966.sol:
The equation of the ellipse is $9x^2 + 16y^2 = 144$.

Dividing by $144$, we get $\dfrac{x^2}{16} + \dfrac{y^2}{9} = 1$.

Here, $a^2 = 16 and b^2 = 9$.

The equation of the line is $3x + 4y + k = 0$, which can be written as $y = -\dfrac{3}{4}x - \dfrac{k}{4}$.

Comparing with $y = mx + c$, we get $m = -\dfrac{3}{4}$ and $c = -\dfrac{k}{4}$.

The condition for the line $y = mx + c$ to touch the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$ is $c^2 = a^2m^2 + b^2$.

Substituting the values, we get:

$\left(-\dfrac{k}{4}\right)^2 = 16\left(-\dfrac{3}{4}\right)^2 + 9$

$\dfrac{k^2}{16} = 16\left(\dfrac{9}{16}\right) + 9$

$\dfrac{k^2}{16} = 9 + 9 = 18$

$k^2 = 18 \times 16 = 288$

$k = \pm 12\sqrt{2}$

Answer: $\mp 12\sqrt{2}$

Therefore, the integrand becomes \text{cosec}^{-1}(\text{cosec}\theta) = \theta.

The integral transforms to:

Applying integration by parts, taking \theta as the first function and 2a\tan$\theta\sec^2$\theta as the second function:

62182.text: If $f(x) and g(x)$ are integrable functions then $\left[\int f(x)dx\right]\left[\int g(x)dx\right] = $
62182.sol:
Let $u = \int f(x)dx$ and $v = \int g(x)dx$.

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get $\dfrac{du}{dx} = f(x)$ and $\dfrac{dv}{dx} = g(x)$.

Using the product rule of differentiation, $\dfrac{d}{dx}(uv) = u\dfrac{dv}{dx} + v\dfrac{du}{dx}$.

Substituting the expressions for $u$, $v$, $\dfrac{du}{dx}$, and $\dfrac{dv}{dx}$, we get $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\left(\int f(x)dx\right)\left(\int g(x)dx\right)\right] = \left(\int f(x)dx\right)g(x) + \left(\int g(x)dx\right)f(x)$.

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain $\left[\int f(x)dx\right]\left[\int g(x)dx\right] = \int \left[f(x)\int g(x)dx + g(x)\int f(x)dx\right]dx$.

Answer: $\int \left[f(x)\int g(x)dx + g(x)\int f(x)dx\right]dx$

$\sum x_i P(x_i) = 1.3$

$0(q) + 1(p) + 2(0.3) + 3(2p) = 1.3$

$p + 0.6 + 6p = 1.3$

$7p = 0.7 \Rightarrow p = 0.1$

Substituting the value of $p$ in the first equation:

$q + 3(0.1) = 0.7$

$q = 0.4$

Thus, $P(X=0) = 0.4$.

Answer: $0.4$

64378.subject: Mathematics
64378.text: The vector equation of the line whose cartesian equations are $x = 2, 2y - 3z + 7 = 0$
64378.sol:
The given cartesian equations of the line are $x = 2$ and $2y - 3z + 7 = 0$.

We can rewrite these equations in symmetric form to find a point on the line and its direction ratios.

$x = 2 \Rightarrow x - 2 = 0 \Rightarrow \dfrac{x - 2}{0}$

$2y - 3z + 7 = 0 \Rightarrow 2y = 3z - 7 \Rightarrow \dfrac{y - 0}{3} = \dfrac{z - \dfrac{7}{3}}{2}$

Equating them, we get the symmetric form of the line:

$\dfrac{x - 2}{0} = \dfrac{y - 0}{3} = \dfrac{z - \dfrac{7}{3}}{2}$

This shows that the line passes through the point with position vector $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} + 0\hat{j} + \dfrac{7}{3}\hat{k}$ and is parallel to the vector $\vec{b} = 0\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$.

The vector equation of the line is given by $\vec{r} = \vec{a} + \lambda \vec{b}$.

Substituting the values of $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$, we get:

$\vec{r} = \left(2\hat{i} + \dfrac{7}{3}\hat{k}\right) + \lambda(3\hat{j} + 2\hat{k})$

Answer: $\vec{r} = \left(2\hat{i} + \dfrac{7}{3}\hat{k}\right) + \lambda(3\hat{j} + 2\hat{k})$

64408.subject: Mathematics
64408.text: If the lines $\dfrac{x-1}{2} = \dfrac{y+1}{3} = \dfrac{z-1}{4}$ and $\dfrac{x-2}{1} = \dfrac{y+m}{2} = \dfrac{z-2}{1}$ intersect each other, then the value of $m$ is....
64408.sol:
Let the given lines be $L_1$ and $L_2$.

Any point on $L_1$ is given by $(2r_1 + 1, 3r_1 - 1, 4r_1 + 1)$.

Any point on $L_2$ is given by $(r_2 + 2, 2r_2 - m, r_2 + 2)$.

For the lines to intersect, these points must coincide for some values of $r_1$ and $r_2$. Equating the $x$, $y$, and $z$ coordinates:

$2r_1 + 1 = r_2 + 2 \Rightarrow 2r_1 - r_2 = 1$

$3r_1 - 1 = 2r_2 - m \Rightarrow 3r_1 - 2r_2 = 1 - m$

$4r_1 + 1 = r_2 + 2 \Rightarrow 4r_1 - r_2 = 1$

Solving the first and third equations:

$4r_1 - r_2 = 1$

$2r_1 - r_2 = 1$

Subtracting the two equations gives $2r_1 = 0 \Rightarrow r_1 = 0$.

Substituting $r_1 = 0$ in $2r_1 - r_2 = 1$ gives $r_2 = -1$.

Substituting $r_1 = 0$ and $r_2 = -1$ in the second equation:

$3(0) - 2(-1) = 1 - m$

$2 = 1 - m$

$m = -1$

Answer: $-1$

64491.text: A plane passes through $(1,-2,1)$ and is perpendicular to the planes $2 x-2 \mathrm{y}+\mathrm{z}=0$ and $x-\mathrm{y}+2 \mathrm{z}=4$. The distance of the point $(1,2,2)$ from this plane is _______ units.

Find the plane perpendicular to both given planes and passing through $(1, -2, 1)$.
The required plane's normal vector $\mathrm{n}$ is perpendicular to normals $\mathrm{n_1} = (2, -2, 1)$ and $\mathrm{n_2} = (1, -1, 2)$, so $\mathrm{n} = \mathrm{n_1} \times \mathrm{n_2} = ( -3, -3, 0 )$, which simplifies to $(1, 1, 0)$.

Using point-normal form with $(1, -2, 1)$: $1(x - 1) + 1(y + 2) + 0(z - 1) = 0$ simplifies to $x + y + 1 = 0$.

Compute the distance from point $(1, 2, 2)$ to the plane.
The distance formula gives $d = \frac{|1 \cdot 1 + 1 \cdot 2 + 0 \cdot 2 + 1|}{\sqrt{1^2 + 1^2 + 0^2}} = \frac{4}{\sqrt{2}} = 2\sqrt{2}$.

$2\sqrt{2}$ corresponds to option C.

65549.text: In a series LCR circuit alternating e.m.f. and current are given by the equations $V = V_0\sin(\omega t)$ and $I = I_0\sin \left(\omega$t + $\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) respectively. The average power dissipated in the circuit over one cycle of a.c. is $(\cos 60^{}^{\circ} = 0.5)
65549.sol:
The given equations for alternating e.m.f. and current are:

$V = V_0 \sin(\omega t)$

$I = I_0 \sin \left(\omega$t + $\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)

The phase difference between$ the voltage and current is\phi =$\dfrac{\pi}{3} =60^{}^{\circ}$.

The average power dissipated in an a.c. circuit over one cycle is given by:

$P_{avg} = V_{rms} I_{rms} \cos \phi$

Substituting $V_{rms} = \dfrac{V_0}{\sqrt{2}}$ and I_{rms} = $\dfrac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}}:

$ P_{avg} = $\left(\dfrac{V_0}{\sqrt{2}}\right) \left(\dfrac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}}\right) \cos60^{}^{\circ}$

Since $\cos 60^{}^{\circ} = \dfrac{1}{2}:

$ P_{avg} = $\dfrac{V_0 I_0}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{V_0 I_0}{4}

Answer: \dfrac{V_0 I_0}{4}$

67210.subject: Physics
67210.text: The speed with which the earth would have to rotate about its axis so that a person on the equator would weigh $\dfrac{3}{5}$ th as much as at present is ($g$ = gravitational acceleration, $R$ = equatorial radius of the earth.)
67210.sol:
The apparent acceleration due to gravity at the equator when the Earth rotates with angular speed $\omega$ is given by:

$g' = g - R\omega^2$

The present weight of a person at the equator is approximately $mg$ (neglecting the small effect of the Earth's current rotation). The new weight is given as $\dfrac{3}{5}$ of the present weight.

$mg' = \dfrac{3}{5}mg$

$g' = \dfrac{3}{5}g$

Substituting the expression for $g'$:

$g - R\omega^2 = \dfrac{3}{5}g$

$R\omega^2 = g - \dfrac{3}{5}g$

$R\omega^2 = \dfrac{2}{5}g$

$\omega^2 = \dfrac{2g}{5R}$

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{2g}{5R}}$

Answer: $\sqrt{\dfrac{2g}{5R}}$

67217.text: The density of a planet is three times that of earth and radius $2.5$ times that of earth. If $g_p$ and $g_e$ represents acceleration due to gravity on planet and earth respectively then ratio $g_p$ to $g_e$ is
67217.sol:
The acceleration due to gravity on the surface of a planet is given by

$g = \dfrac{GM}{R^2}$

Substituting the mass of the planet $M = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3 \rho$, we get

$g = \dfrac{G}{R^2} \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3 \rho\right) = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi G R \rho$

This implies that $g \propto R \rho$.

The ratio of acceleration due to gravity on the planet to that on Earth is

$\dfrac{g_p}{g_e} = \dfrac{R_p \rho_p}{R_e \rho_e}$

Given that $\rho_p = 3\rho_e$ and $R_p = 2.5R_e$, substituting these values yields

$\dfrac{g_p}{g_e} = (2.5) \times (3) = 7.5$

Answer: $7.5$

68112.subject: Physics
68112.text: Under isothermal condition, two soap bubbles of radii $r_1$ and $r_2$ combine to form a single soap bubble of radius R. The surface tension of the soap solution is (P = outside pressure)
68112.sol:
Let $T$ be the surface tension of the soap solution.

The pressure inside a soap bubble of radius $r$ is given by $P_i = P + \dfrac{4T}{r}$, where $P$ is the outside pressure.

The volume of the bubble is $V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$.

Under isothermal conditions, the temperature remains constant. The total number of moles of air inside the bubbles is conserved, which gives $P_1 V_1 + P_2 V_2 = P_f V_f$.

Substituting the values for the two initial bubbles and the final bubble:

$\left(P + \dfrac{4T}{r_1}\right) \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r_1^3 + \left(P + \dfrac{4T}{r_2}\right) \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r_2^3 = \left(P + \dfrac{4T}{R}\right) \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3$

Dividing the entire equation by $\dfrac{4}{3}\pi$:

$P r_1^3 + 4T r_1^2 + P r_2^3 + 4T r_2^2 = P R^3 + 4T R^2$

Rearranging the terms to solve for $T$:

$4T r_1^2 + 4T r_2^2 - 4T R^2 = P R^3 - P r_1^3 - P r_2^3$

$4T (r_1^2 + r_2^2 - R^2) = P (R^3 - r_1^3 - r_2^3)$

$T = \dfrac{P(R^3 - r_1^3 - r_2^3)}{4(r_1^2 + r_2^2 - R^2)}$

Answer: $\dfrac{P(R^3 - r_1^3 - r_2^3)}{4(r_1^2 + r_2^2 - R^2)}$

70936.text: Select the INCORRECT statement related to Biological Diversity Act.
options: The government passed Biological Diversity Act in the year 2002 in compliance with CBD.

70936.sol:
The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 defines biological resources as plants, animals, and micro-organisms or parts thereof, their genetic material and by-products with actual or potential use or value.

The definition explicitly excludes value-added products and human genetic material.

Therefore, the statement that it includes value-added products and human genetic material is incorrect.

Answer: It includes value added products and human genetic material.

70940.text: Identify the correct order of known species of organisms by their increasing numbers.
70940.sol:
The approximate number of known and described species for different groups of organisms is as follows:

Eubacteria: $\sim 10,000$
Protists: $\sim 60,000$
Fungi: $\sim 100,000$
Plants: $\sim 300,000$
Animals: $ > 1,200,000$

Arranging them in increasing order of their known species numbers, we get:
Eubacteria \rightarrow Protists \rightarrow Fungi \rightarrow Plants \rightarrow Animals.

71017.subject: Biology
71017.text: Arrange the following organs of the Human respiratory system from outside to inside:
options: Lungs, pleural membranes, thoracic cavity, alveoli
Thoracic cavity, lungs, pleural membranes, alveoli
Thoracic cavity, pleural membranes, lungs, alveoli
Thoracic cavity, lungs, alveoli, pleural membranes
71017.sol:
The human respiratory system is situated in the thoracic cavity, which is the outermost structure among the given options.

Inside the thoracic cavity, the lungs are present. The lungs are enclosed by a double-layered pleura (pleural membranes), consisting of an outer parietal pleura in contact with the thoracic lining and an inner visceral pleura in contact with the lung surface. Therefore, the pleural membranes are encountered after the thoracic cavity and before the main lung tissue.

Deep inside the lungs, the terminal bronchioles open into thin-walled, vascularised bag-like structures called alveoli.

Thus, the correct arrangement from outside to inside is: Thoracic cavity, pleural membranes, lungs, alveoli.

Answer: Thoracic cavity, pleural membranes, lungs, alveoli

71183.subject: Biology
71183.text:
Identify the CORRECT statement about CLEAVAGE in HUMAN ZYGOTE.
Statement (I): Cleavage is holoblastic.
Statement (II): First cleavage is meridional.
Statement (III): Second cleavage is horizontal.
Statement (IV): Third cleavage is horizontal.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: I, II and III are correct
I, II and IV are correct
Only I and II are correct
71183.sol:
Cleavage in the human zygote is holoblastic because the egg is almost alecithal or microlecithal, meaning it contains very little yolk. Thus, Statement I is correct.

The first cleavage division is meridional, passing through the animal-vegetal axis to form two blastomeres. Thus, Statement II is correct.

Mammals exhibit rotational cleavage. During the second cleavage, one blastomere divides meridionally while the other divides equatorially. Therefore, stating the second cleavage is purely horizontal is incorrect. Thus, Statement III is incorrect.

Subsequent cleavages in mammals are highly asynchronous and do not follow a strict synchronized pattern of horizontal or equatorial planes as seen in amphibians. The typical generalized third horizontal cleavage does not apply to the human embryo. Thus, Statement IV is incorrect.

Therefore, only statements I and II are correct.

Answer: Only I and II are correct

71239.subject: Biology
71239.text: Which of the following groups has all three micro-elements?
71239.sol:
Macronutrients are generally present in plant tissues in large amounts (in excess of $10 \text{ mmole kg}^{-1}$ of dry matter). The macronutrients include carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorous, sulphur, potassium, calcium and magnesium.

Micronutrients or trace elements are needed in very small amounts (less than $10 \text{ mmole kg}^{-1}$ of dry matter). These include iron, manganese, copper, molybdenum, zinc, boron, chlorine and nickel.

Analyzing the given options:
Magnesium (Mg), Potassium (K), Sulphur (S), and Calcium (Ca) are macronutrients.
Therefore, the groups in the first, third, and fourth options contain macronutrients.

Zinc (Zn) and Copper (Cu) are micronutrients, and Silicon (Si) is a beneficial trace element required by some higher plants. Since it does not contain any macronutrients, this is the most appropriate choice.

Answer: Zinc, Copper, Silicon

71585.subject: Chemistry
71585.text: Identify the product formed when ethyl alcohol reacts with $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ at 443 K.
71585.sol:
When ethyl alcohol is heated with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ at $443\text{ K}$, it undergoes intramolecular dehydration to form ethene.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow[443\text{ K}]{\text{conc. H}_2\text{SO}_4} \text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

At a lower temperature of $413\text{ K}$, intermolecular dehydration occurs to yield ethoxyethane (diethyl ether).

Thus, the product formed at $443\text{ K}$ is ethene.

Answer: Ethene

71720.subject: Chemistry
71720.text: What is the role of aspirin?
71720.sol:
Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) belongs to the class of drugs known as non-narcotic analgesics.

It is primarily used to relieve skeletal pain, such as that due to arthritis, by inhibiting the synthesis of chemicals called prostaglandins, which stimulate inflammation in the tissues and cause pain. It also has antipyretic (fever-reducing) properties.

Thus, the primary role of aspirin is as an analgesic.

Answer: Analgesics

71986.subject: Chemistry
71986.text:
Identify the correct statements for ideal solution.
(A) It obeys Raoult's law over the entire range of concentration.
(B) It shows a positive deviation from Raoult's law.
(C) In an ideal solution, solvent-solute, solute-solute and solvent-solvent molecular interactions are comparable.
(D) The volume change i.e. $\Delta_{\text{mix}}V = 0$
(E) The enthalpy change i.e. $\Delta_{\text{mix}}H = 0$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
71986.sol:
An ideal solution is defined as a solution that obeys Raoult's law over the entire range of concentration. Thus, statement (A) is correct and statement (B) is incorrect.

For an ideal solution, the intermolecular attractive forces between the solute-solute and solvent-solvent molecules are nearly equal to those between solute-solvent molecules. Thus, statement (C) is correct.

Since the interactions are similar, there is no change in volume or enthalpy upon mixing. Therefore, $\Delta_{\text{mix}}V = 0$ and $\Delta_{\text{mix}}H = 0$. Thus, statements (D) and (E) are correct.

The correct statements are (A), (C), (D) and (E).

Answer: (A), (C), (D) and (E) only.

72043.text: 1 mole of certain gas expands isothermally and reversibly from 1 dm^3$ to 10 dm^3$ and performs $-4308$ J work. Calculate the temperature at which expansion of gas takes place [R = 8.314 JK^{-1}$ mol^{-1}$]
72043.sol:
For an isothermal reversible expansion, the work done is given by:

$W = -2.303 n R T \log_{10} \left( \dfrac{V_2}{V_1} \right)

Substituting the given values $ W = -4308$ J, $n = 1$ mol, $R = 8.314$ J K^{-1}$ mol^{-1}$, $V_1 = 1$ dm^3$, and $V_2 = 10$ dm$^3$:

$-4308 = -2.303 \times1 \times8.314 \times$ T $\times \log_{10} \left( \dfrac{10}{1} \right)

$-4308 = -19.147 $\times$ T $\times1$

$T = \dfrac{4308}{19.147}

$ T $\approx225$ K

Answer: $225$ K.

72106.subject: Physics
72106.text: The radius of the orbit of an electron in a hydrogen like atom is $4.5a_0$, where $a_0$ is the Bohr radius. Its orbital angular momentum is $\dfrac{3h}{2\pi}$. It is given than h is Planck's constant and R is Rydberg's constant. The possible wavelength $(\lambda)$, when the transition of atom from higher energy level to lower energy level, is
72106.sol:
The orbital angular momentum of an electron is given by $L = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$.

Given $L = \dfrac{3h}{2\pi}$, we get $n = 3$.

The radius of the $n$-th orbit in a hydrogen-like atom is $r = \dfrac{n^2}{Z}a_0$.

Substituting $r = 4.5a_0 and n = 3$:

$4.5a_0 = \dfrac{3^2}{Z}a_0 \Rightarrow Z = \dfrac{9}{4.5} = 2$

The possible transitions from the $n = 3$ state to lower energy levels are $n = 3 \rightarrow 1 and n = 3 \rightarrow 2$.

Using the Rydberg formula for wavelength:

$\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = RZ^2 \left( \dfrac{1}{n_f^2} - \dfrac{1}{n_i^2} \right)

For the transition $ n = 3 → 1$:

\dfrac{1}{\lambda} =$ R(2)^2 $\left( \dfrac{1}{1^2} - \dfrac{1}{3^2} \right) =4R \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{9} \right) =4R \left( \dfrac{8}{9} \right) = \dfrac{32R}{9}

$\lambda = $\dfrac{9}{32R}

For$ the transition n = 3 → 2$:

\dfrac{1}{\lambda} =$ R(2)^2 $\left( \dfrac{1}{2^2} - \dfrac{1}{3^2} \right) =4R \left( \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{9} \right) =4R \left( \dfrac{5}{36} \right) = \dfrac{5R}{9}

$\lambda = $\dfrac{9}{5R}

Among$ the given options,$\dfrac{9}{32R}$ is a possible wavelength.

Answer: $\dfrac{9}{32R}$

72499.text: A boy stands $x\ \text{m}$ away from a high wall and claps his hands at a steady rate so that each clap coincides with the echo of the one before. If he makes $60$ claps in $2$ minutes and the velocity of sound is $340\ \text{m/s}$, then the distance $x$ from the wall is
72499.sol:
Time taken for $60$ claps is $2$ minutes $= 120\ \text{s}$.

Time interval between two consecutive claps is $T = \dfrac{120}{60} = 2\ \text{s}$.

Let the distance of the boy from the wall be $x$. The sound travels a distance of $2x$ (to the wall and back) to form an echo.

Time taken for the echo to return is $t = \dfrac{2x}{v}$.

Since each clap coincides with the echo of the previous one, the time for the echo to return equals the time interval between claps, so $t = T$.

$\dfrac{2x}{340} = 2$

$2x = 680$

$x = 340\ \text{m}$

Answer: $340\ \text{m}$

Graphite is the thermodynamically most stable allotrope of carbon at standard temperature and pressure.

The standard enthalpy of formation, $\Delta_{f}H^{{}^{\circ}}$, for graphite is taken as zero.

Coal is an amorphous form of carbon and is also less stable than graphite.

For $\langle 1, 3, 2 angle$, $2(1) + 3(3) + 2 = 13 eq 0$

For $\langle 2, 2, -10 angle$, $2(2) + 3(2) - 10 = 0$

79258.subject: Mathematics
79258.text:
Passage: Let $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$, $\vec{c}$ be unit vectors. Further, $\vec{a}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{b}$; $\vec{c}$ makes an angle $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ with both $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$; and $\vec{c}=p\vec{a}+q\vec{b}+r(\vec{a}\times\vec{b})$.

Question: What is the value of $(p+q)$ ?
79258.sol:
Given $|\vec{a}| = |\vec{b}| = |\vec{c}| = 1$ and $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = 0$.

Since $\vec{c}$ makes an angle $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ with both $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$:

$\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a} = |\vec{c}||\vec{a}|\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\vec{c} \cdot \vec{b} = |\vec{c}||\vec{b}|\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

We are given the relation:

$\vec{c} = p\vec{a} + q\vec{b} + r(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$

Taking the dot product of both sides with $\vec{a}$:

$\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a} = p(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{a}) + q(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{a}) + r((\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{a})$

Since $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{a} = 1$, $\vec{b} \cdot \vec{a} = 0$, and $(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{a} = 0$, we get:

$p = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Taking the dot product of both sides with $\vec{b}$:

$\vec{c} \cdot \vec{b} = p(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}) + q(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{b}) + r((\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{b})$

Since $\vec{b} \cdot \vec{b} = 1$, $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = 0$, and $(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{b} = 0$, we get:

$q = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Therefore, $p + q = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} = 1$.

Answer: $1$

83468.subject: Physics
83468.text: A solid cylinder of mass $M$ and radius $R$ rolls without slipping on an inclined plane of length $L$ and height $h$. What is the speed of its centre of mass when the cylinder reaches its bottom?
83468.sol:
Here K.E. of centre of mass when cylinder reached the bottom $=\frac{1}{2} m v^2+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{I} \omega^2 \ldots(\mathrm{i})$
Here $\mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{2} M K^2$ and $\omega=\frac{V}{R}$
$\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \mathrm{KE}=\frac{1}{2} m v^2+\frac{1}{2} M K^2 \cdot \frac{V^2}{r^2} \\
& =\frac{1}{2} m v^2\left[1+\frac{K^2}{R^2}\right]
\end{aligned}$
But for solid cylinder $K=\frac{R}{\sqrt{2}}$ or $\frac{K^2}{R^2}=\frac{1}{2}$
$\therefore K E=\frac{3}{4} m v^2$
PE of the solid cylinder at height $h$ is
$\mathrm{PE}=m g h$
From eq. (ii) and (iii)
$\begin{aligned}
& m g h=\frac{3}{4} m v^2 \\
& \Rightarrow v=\sqrt{\frac{4}{3} g h}
\end{aligned}$

83752.subject: Physics
83752.text: The intensity at the maximum in a Young's double slit experiment is ${I}_{0}$. Distance between two slits is $d = 5\lambda$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength of light used in the experiment. What will be the intensity in front of one of the slits on the screen placed at a distance $D = 10d$?
83752.sol:
In YDSE ${I}_{max} = {I}_{0}$

Path difference at a point in front of one of shifts is

$∆ x = d\left(\dfrac{y}{D}\right) = d\left(\dfrac{\dfrac{d}{2}}{D}\right) = \dfrac{{d}^{2}}{2D}$ $( Herey = \dfrac{d}{2} )$

$∆ x = \dfrac{{d}^{2}}{2\left(10d\right)} = \dfrac{d}{20} = \dfrac{5\lambda}{20} = \dfrac{\lambda}{4}$

Path difference is

$ϕ = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda}\Deltax = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda}\left(\dfrac{\lambda}{4}\right)$

$ϕ = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

So intensity at that point is

$I = {I}_{max}\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)$

$I = {I}_{0}\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{{I}_{0}}{2}$

85138.subject: Zoology
options: two different parasites on the same host
sharing of one or more resources between the two species
85138.sol:
Niche/ecological niche is a specific part of habitat occupied by individuals of a species which is circumscribed by its range of tolerance, range of movement, microclimate, type of food and its availability, shelter, type of predator and timing of activity. Habitat has several ecological niches and supports a numbe of species. An ecological niche is used by a single species. Two or more species cannot use the same niche despite having a mutualistic association. Organism or populations in the competition have a niche overlap of a limited resource fo which they compete. Both owl and cat feed on shrews and mice. They occupy the same niche because of being ecological equivalents though their habitats are different.
So, the correct answer is 'Sharing of one or more resources between the two species'.

85146.subject: Zoology
85146.sol:
A mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association between a green plant and a fungus. The plant makes organic molecules such as sugars by photosynthesis and supplies them to the fungus, and the fungus supplies to the plant water and mineral nutrients, such as phosphorus, taken from the soil.
Related Theory
Mycorrhizae permits the plant to obtain additional moisture and nutrients. When mycorrhizae are present, plants are less susceptible to water stress.

TURNER’s SYNDROME:

Introduction: It was first described in 1938 by Turner. The disorder develops due to monosomy of the sex chromosome. The disease is seen only in females. It is an allosomal chromosomal abnormality.
Cause: The disorder is due to monosomy. It appears due to fusion of abnormal egg (22+0) and a normal sperm (22+X) or a normal egg (22+X) and abnormal sperm (22+0).

Karyotype: [44 + XO]

Symptoms:
1. Short stature.
2. Webbed neck.
3. Flat and broad chest.
4. Rudimentary ovaries (defective ovaries, no production of ova). Sterility in females.
5. No Barr bodies.
6. Average to normal I.Q.

88024.subject: Chemistry
88024.text:
Which one of the following statements are true?
$( 1 )$ Transition metals form alloys
$( 2 )$ Transition metals form complexes
$( 3 )$ Zn, Cd and Hg are transition metals
$( 4 ){K}_{2} \left[PtC{l}_{6}\right] is a well known compound, but corresponding nickel compound is not known.$
88024.sol:
Here statement (3) is not true as Zn, Cd and Hg are not regarded transition metals, because the neutral atoms as well as stable ions have fully-filled d-orbitals.
Statements (1), (2) and (4) are true as transition metals have similar atomic sized, therefore, in the crystal lattice, one transition metals atoms can be easily replaced by the atoms of another transition metal to form alloy. They can easily form complexes, because they form small highly charged cations, which have vacant orbitals of suitable energy to accept electron pairs donated by ligands.
As the sum of first four ionization energies of Pt is less than the sum of first four ionization energies of Ni, so ${K}_{2} \left[PtC{l}_{6}\right] is more stable than the corresponding nickel compound.$

There will be an increase in the number of detritivores
Herbivores will not receive solar energy
The movement of minerals in an ecosystem will be blocked.
96594.sol: Thee organic content of the dead and decaying organisms are broken down to inorganic substances by the process called decomposition. It is brought about by decomposers. Decomposition is mainly an oxygen dependent process and its rate is dependent on chemical composition and climatic factors. Decomposers play a vital role in energy flow through the ecosystem and also in making available the essential nutrients to the producers. If decomposers are removed from the ecosystem, then minerals required by the producers will not be available and disrupt the food chain.

100094.subject: Physics
100094.text:
Consider a system of units where the standard unit of length is doubled and the standard unit of time is halved, while the unit of mass remains unchanged. Read the following statements regarding the new units of derived quantities:

(A) The unit of velocity becomes $4$ times its original value.
(B) The unit of acceleration becomes $8$ times its original value.
(C) The unit of momentum becomes $4$ times its original value.
(D) The unit of force becomes $4$ times its original value.

How many of the above statements are correct?
100094.sol:
Let the original units of mass, length, and time be $M$, $L$, and $T$.
The new units are $M' = M$, $L' = 2L$, and $T' = T/2$.

Evaluating each statement using dimensional formulas:

(A) Velocity $[LT^{-1}]$: The new unit is $L'(T')^{-1} = (2L)(T/2)^{-1} = 4[LT^{-1}]$. Statement (A) is correct.

(B) Acceleration $[LT^{-2}]$: The new unit is $L'(T')^{-2} = (2L)(T/2)^{-2} = 8[LT^{-2}]$. Statement (B) is correct.

(C) Momentum $[MLT^{-1}]$: The new unit is $M'L'(T')^{-1} = M(2L)(T/2)^{-1} = 4[MLT^{-1}]$. Statement (C) is correct.

(D) Force $[MLT^{-2}]$: The new unit is $M'L'(T')^{-2} = M(2L)(T/2)^{-2} = 8[MLT^{-2}]$. Statement (D) is incorrect (it becomes $8$ times, not $4$ times).

Therefore, exactly three statements are correct.

Answer: Only three

100440.subject: Physics
100440.text:
A body is projected horizontally from the top of a tower of height $180 \mathrm{~m}$ with a velocity of $20 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$. If acceleration due to gravity is $10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$, then match the following.
$\begin{array}{llll}A & B & C & D\end{array}$
100440.sol:
Given, initial horizontal component of velocity,
$u_x=20 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \text{. }$
Initial vertical component of velocity,
$u_y=0$
Acceleration due to gravity,
$g=a_y=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$
So, horizontal component of velocity after $1 \mathrm{~s}$,
$\begin{aligned}
v_x & =u_x+a_x t \\
& =20+0=20 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}$
and vertical component of velocity after $1 \mathrm{~s}$,
$\begin{aligned}
v_y & =u_y+a_y t \\
& =0+10 \times 1 \\
& =10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}$
Horizontal displacement after $1 \mathrm{~s}$,
$\begin{aligned}
s_X & =u_x t+\frac{1}{2} a_X t^2 \\
& =20 \times 1+0=20 \mathrm{~m}
\end{aligned}$
Vertical displacement after $1 \mathrm{~s}$,
$\begin{aligned}
s_y & =u_y t+\frac{1}{2} a_y t^2 \\
& =0+\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times(1)^2=5 \mathrm{~m}
\end{aligned}$
Resultant velocity after $1 \mathrm{~s}$,
$\begin{aligned}
v= & \sqrt{v_x^2+v_y^2} \\
= & \sqrt{(20)^2+(10)^2}=\sqrt{400+100}=\sqrt{500} \\
& =22.36=22.4 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s},
\end{aligned}$
So, the correct option is (c).

100506.subject: Physics
100506.text: A uniform solid cylinder and a uniform solid sphere, having the same mass and the same radius, are free to rotate about their respective central axes. If the same constant torque is applied to both for the same time duration starting from rest, what will be the ratio of the final angular velocity of the solid cylinder to that of the solid sphere?
100506.sol:
Let the mass of both objects be $M$ and their radius be $R$.

The moment of inertia of a uniform solid cylinder about its central axis is $I_{cyl} = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^2$.

The moment of inertia of a uniform solid sphere about its central axis is $I_{sph} = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2$.

From Newton's second law for rotation, the angular acceleration is given by $\alpha = \dfrac{\tau}{I}$.

Since both objects start from rest, their final angular velocity after time $t$ is $\omega = \alpha t = \dfrac{\tau t}{I}$.

Given that the applied torque $\tau$ and time $t$ are the same for both, the angular velocity is inversely proportional to the moment of inertia ($\omega \propto \dfrac{1}{I}$).

Therefore, the ratio of their angular velocities is:
$\dfrac{\omega_{cyl}}{\omega_{sph}} = \dfrac{I_{sph}}{I_{cyl}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{2}{5}MR^2}{\dfrac{1}{2}MR^2} = \dfrac{2}{5} \times \dfrac{2}{1} = \dfrac{4}{5}$

The ratio is $4 : 5$.

Answer: $4 : 5$

102879.subject: Physics
102879.text: Two infinitely long, thin straight wires, each carrying a uniform positive linear charge density $+\lambda$, are placed along the X and Y axes respectively in free space. What is the magnitude of the net electric field at a point $P(a, a)$ in the XY plane?
102879.sol:
The point $P(a, a)$ is at a perpendicular distance $a$ from the X-axis and a perpendicular distance $a$ from the Y-axis.

The electric field due to the wire along the X-axis at point $P$ is directed along the positive Y-direction:
$\vec{E}_1 = \dfrac{\lambda}{2\pi\epsilon_0 a} \hat{j}$

The electric field due to the wire along the Y-axis at point $P$ is directed along the positive X-direction:
$\vec{E}_2 = \dfrac{\lambda}{2\pi\epsilon_0 a} \hat{i}$

Since these two electric field vectors are perpendicular to each other, the magnitude of the net electric field is given by vector addition:
$E_{net} = \sqrt{E_1^2 + E_2^2}$

$E_{net} = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{\lambda}{2\pi\epsilon_0 a}\right)^2 + \left(\dfrac{\lambda}{2\pi\epsilon_0 a}\right)^2}$

$E_{net} = \sqrt{2} \left(\dfrac{\lambda}{2\pi\epsilon_0 a}\right) = \dfrac{\lambda}{\sqrt{2}\pi\epsilon_0 a}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\lambda}{\sqrt{2}\pi\epsilon_0 a}$

103787.text: An electron is travelling along the $x$-direction. It encounters a magnetic field in the $y$-direction. Its subsequent motion will be
options: a circle in the $x z$ plane
a circle in the $y z$ plane
a circle in the $x y$ plane.
103787.sol:
We know that the force on a charged particle $e$ due to a magnetic field is given by

$ \begin{array}{ll} 
& \vec{F}=e(\vec{v} \times \vec{B}) \\
\text{ Here } \vec{v}=v_x=\hat{i} \text{ and } \vec{B}=B_y \hat{j} \\
\therefore \quad & \vec{F}=e v_x B_y(\hat{i} \times \hat{j})=e v_x B_y \hat{k}
\end{array} $
Therefore the subsequent motion of the charged particle will be a circle in the $x z$ plane.

So, A,C,D are true but B is false.
